questions.q: Where do the Helm charts for product-catalog and checkout live in the storefront monorepo?
options: Inside each service's own services/<name>/ folder
In a separate repository dedicated to Helm charts
Under charts/product-catalog/ and charts/checkout/ at the repo root
Inside .github/workflows/ alongside the pipeline definitions
questions.explain: The monorepo layout keeps Helm charts at charts/product-catalog/ and charts/checkout/, separate from the application code under services/ and the pipeline definitions under .github/workflows/.

questions.q: What does "trunk-based development" mean for how main is treated?
options: main is rebuilt from scratch before every release
main is always deployable, so there are no long-lived branches that drift out of sync
main is only updated once per quarter
main is where feature branches live permanently
questions.explain: Trunk-based development means main is always deployable. Engineers work on short-lived feature branches rather than long-lived branches that could drift far out of sync with main.

questions.q: What are the two required conditions before a feature branch PR can merge into main?
options: A passing linter only, with no human review required
At least 1 reviewer approval and passing CI
Two reviewer approvals and a signed changelog entry
Only that the branch name follows the feature/<ticket> convention
questions.explain: Branch protection on main requires at least one reviewer approval and passing CI (lint, tests, build, Trivy, gitleaks) before a PR can merge, and merges happen via squash merge.

questions.q: What specifically triggers an automatic deploy to the northbridge-staging namespace?
options: Any merge to main, same as dev
Pushing a semver tag such as v1.4.0
A manual click in the GitHub Environments UI
Opening a pull request against main
questions.explain: Promotion to staging is tag-based: a maintainer cuts a semver tag like v1.4.0, which automatically deploys that build to the northbridge-staging namespace. Merges to main only deploy to dev.

questions.q: What stands between a successful staging deploy and a deploy to northbridge-prod?
options: Nothing — staging success auto-promotes to prod
A second full CI run from scratch
A manual approval gate enforced by a GitHub Environments protection rule requiring 1 reviewer
A new feature branch must be opened
questions.explain: Production promotion requires a manual approval gate — a GitHub Environments protection rule with one required reviewer — before the helm upgrade to the northbridge-prod namespace runs.
